title: Constructors

youtube.title: C++ Constructors: Start Every Object Right | C++ Programming EP 53
youtube.description: In this episode you will write a constructor, write several constructors and explain the default constructor, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Constructors · 0:55 Constructors · 1:35 Which constructor runs? · 2:05 Second program · 3:05 Recap · 3:35 Bug of the Day · 4:23 Challenge · 4:43 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "CONSTRUCTORS" in tomato on peach; Xecxec next to a factory that builds a ready toy; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a factory that builds a ready toy

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we make objects that start in a good state. A constructor runs the moment an object is born.

scenes.onScreen: "Constructors": numbered lines (1. A constructor runs when an object is made; 2. It has the class name and no return type; 3. A class can have several constructors) and an analogy card: a new phone: it comes ready, with the setup already done
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A constructor is a special function. It has the same name as the class, and it has no return type. It runs when an object is made. A class can have several constructors with different parameters. If you write none, the compiler gives you an empty default one. If you write any, it does not. Think of a new phone that comes with the setup already done.
points: A constructor runs when an object is made
It has the class name and no return type
A class can have several constructors

analogy.title: Constructors
analogy.body: A new phone: it comes ready, with the setup already done

scenes.onScreen: point.cpp: a Point class with two constructors
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 8] This is the default constructor. It sets both numbers to zero. [HL 9] This constructor takes two values. [HL 10] The show function prints the point. [HL 14] This object uses the default constructor. [HL 15] This object uses the second one. [HL 16] The first prints zero, zero. [HL 17] The second prints three, four.

scenes.onScreen: a table of declarations and the constructor that runs
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: The compiler chooses a constructor by the arguments. No arguments means the default one. Two ints mean the second one. Round brackets and curly braces both work.

diagram.caption: a table of declarations and the constructor that runs

scenes.onScreen: defaults.cpp: one constructor with default values replaces two
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 10] One constructor has two default values. [HL 15] No arguments: the name is Unknown and the age is one. [HL 16] One argument: the age is still one. [HL 17] Two arguments: both defaults are replaced. The output has three lines.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as defaults dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints Unknown one, Moti one, and Kali four.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A constructor runs when an object is made. Two. It has the class name and no return type. Three. A class can have several constructors. Four. Default arguments can replace several constructors. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A constructor runs when an object is made.
It has the class name and no return type.
A class can have several constructors.
Default arguments can replace several constructors.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: No default constructor
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The class has only a two-value constructor. Main makes a point with no values. The compiler says no matching function for call to Point. When you write any constructor, the free default one disappears. Add your own.

scenes.onScreen: The constructor told the object, do not worry. I will get you started.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: The constructor told the object, do not worry. I will get you started.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: write a Rectangle constructor
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write a class called Rectangle with width and height. Add a constructor with two values and a function that returns the area. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: member initializer lists. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

point.cpp: In function 'int main()':
point.cpp:13:11: error: no matching function for call to 'Point::Point()'
   13 |     Point p;
      |           ^
point.cpp:8:5: note: candidate: 'Point::Point(int, int)'
    8 |     Point(int x, int y) : x_(x), y_(y) {}
bug.why: When you write any constructor, the compiler stops making the empty default one. Write your own if you need it.

pun: "The constructor told the object, do not worry. I will get you started."
challenge: Write a class called Rectangle with width and height. Add a constructor with two values and a function that returns the area.
challengeAnswer: Keep the two numbers private. The constructor stores them. The area function returns width times height.
